title: Seoul, it’s a bit familiar this summer
body:
When I opened the weather app today, it was 35℃. The body temperature is 38℃.

I feel like being exposed to the morning sun for just a moment can turn it into medium rare wagyu beef

I recently saw a piece of news that was quite interesting. Of course, South Korea also ate bluefin tuna in the past, but most of it was imported frozen. The freshest ones are basically supplied to Japan.

This year is different. Because of the warming of the sea water, bluefin tuna, which is two meters long and weighs hundreds of kilograms, was rarely seen in the East Sea of ​​South Korea in the past. Now it is becoming more and more common. The fish does not need to cross the ocean. It is still in the sea in the morning, in Lotte Supermarket in the afternoon, and on the dining table in the evening.

As an e-commerce person, my first reaction is not the climate. Rather: the transportation distance is gone, the cold chain costs are gone, and the intermediate links are gone. Unexpectedly, it was not logistics or AI that finally solved the supply chain problem.

It's the climate.

Everyone used to talk about climate change. Reduce emissions, protect the environment, and drive less. There are always people who say: I know, let’s talk about it later.

When a box of fresher and cheaper bluefin tuna was placed in front of me, I discovered that humans change their opinions very quickly.

I suddenly felt a little envious of tuna.

At least it's fresh.

And by the time I got to the subway station from home, I was almost ready.

When I hurried out in the morning, I stuffed half a piece of chocolate into my trouser pocket, thinking of eating it while taking the subway.

After getting in the car, I took out my mobile phone and took out a brown and sticky hand. 😑

At that moment, I was petrified, and then I thought seriously for a few seconds: no paper, no water, and nine stations. You can't just keep this hand raised all the time.

So, I made the most rational decision as an adult - to solve the problem in the most environmentally friendly way.

The Korean passenger opposite me moved from confusion to shock to silently moving back a little.

I guess there was only one sentence in his mind: "What did this person... just take out of his trouser pocket...?"

Later I realized that what really melted just now was not the chocolate, but the social image that I could no longer explain in Korea.

So this week, I decided that the team should not come to the office and let everyone use the air conditioning at home.

It's not for efficiency, I just feel that in this kind of weather, it's not easy for everyone to stay solid on the way to the company. During the few minutes I walked from the subway to the office, I felt like I was about to be transformed into an elixir.

Dare to ask God, that sun switch...can it be turned down a little first? Summer is here, and you have to rely on your coolness to relieve the heat.

Suddenly I felt that if God closed the door and the window for someone, then don’t bother. Because God is ready to turn on the air conditioner….

That's it for now.

If it's hotter, it's rude.

title: A thousand stalls, a thousand interesting souls
body:
I came to Seoul Illustration Fair for the first time today.

At first I thought it was just selling cultural and creative products. After entering, I discovered that there were almost a thousand independent creators inside.

Everyone is painting their own world.

Some people drew foxes, rabbits, and kittens and made them into dolls, keychains, and stickers; some people turned their original characters into umbrellas, T-shirts, mugs, and room decorations; and some people painted on the spot and taught everyone to create together.

I also waited in line for twenty minutes to get in, and there were always people inside.

Then I suddenly understood why there are cute designs everywhere in Korea. Small icons in the subway, reminders on buses, convenience store packaging, coffee shop menus, street corner posters, and even various public signs in the city all have a sense of design that makes people smile.

It turns out it’s not because there are a few great designers. It's because there are countless people painting below. These works may not all become hits, but they give the city a steady stream of new ideas. I love this soil.

Everyone here seems to be encouraged to draw what they like seriously. Some will like it, some won't. It's okay, just draw it first.

There are also many experience areas on site where everyone can sit down and create together. I also drew two small surfboards. Although the drawings look like kindergarten works😂, I don’t feel embarrassed at all.

The biggest gain today is not what I bought. But I saw that the creativity of a city does not come from a few geniuses. It comes from thousands of ordinary people who are willing to take a small idea in their head and turn it into something that others are willing to take home.

This kind of creativity will slowly grow into a culture.

No wonder when walking in Korea, I always feel that even cuteness has a kind of industrial vitality.

There's something joyful that's hard to translate.

But if you walk around, you can feel it.

title: In team building, the most important thing is actually not eating.
body:
Last week, I took the team to a dinner cruise on the Han River.

Every quarter, I will select a few colleagues and give them a small gift.

In July, it was a U.S. Marine Corps badge.

Because of the motto of the United States Marine Corps:

Semper Fidelis (Always Faithful)

Every Marine knows that the people around him are worthy of his life; and he will become the strongest support for others.

The company is certainly not a battlefield. But I have always felt that a truly good team should also have the same trust.

When there is a problem, there is no need to shout, someone will always stand up. Therefore, this badge is never given to the person with the best performance. But give it to those who make others feel more at ease at work.

There is also a little surprise.

It turned out that there was a magician hidden in the team, and he performed several magic tricks during the dinner. Suddenly I feel that the most interesting thing about a team is this.

Some people solve problems, some create surprises; some rush to the front, and some silently support others. Everyone is different.

Just because they are different, the team is more complete.

Thank you to everyone who makes the team better

title: I was at Gyeongpo Lake and didn’t look at the lake all the time.
body:
If someone asks me, what is the most beautiful thing about Gyeongpo Lake?

I probably won't answer Lake.

Of course Gyeongpo Lake is beautiful in summer.

I live on the top floor of Skybay. When I open the window, I can see the East China Sea on one side and Gyeongpo Lake on the other. Sea breeze and lake breeze blow in almost at the same time. In the morning, the lake surface is as flat as a piece of paper; in the evening, the clouds sink little by little, the lotus leaves sway gently, and occasionally a heron flies across the water.

These are beautiful.

But what really stopped me again and again were the little bronze figures by the lake, only thirty or forty centimeters tall.

At first I just took a random photo.

Later it was discovered that every ten meters, there was a new group.

When two young people met for the first time, the boy was so nervous that he didn't know where to put his hands. When he gave flowers, he pretended to be calm, but couldn't help but peek at the girl to see if she was smiling. Later, they fell in love and separated. One chased, the other waited, one secretly shed tears, and the other pretended as if nothing had happened.

Walking further, we met a young man holding a knife, a man on a horse, an old man counting with his fingers, a child being chased by a puppy, a child laughing with his bare buttocks, and a girl crying with tears all over her face...

Each statue is not big, but it seems like a moment has been preserved.

The best thing is the expression.

Some people burst into laughter.

Some people were so shocked that they forgot to close their mouths.

Some people cried with tears etched on their faces.

There was also a child who raised his wooden stick high, as if he was about to smash it down in the next second. I stood there and watched for a long time, and couldn't help laughing.

They are not from the same era as me.

There are scholars and military generals; there are old people and young people.

The clothes and hats are separated by hundreds of years.

There seems to be no difference when you are funny, when you cry, when you like someone.

I rode my bike and looked at each statue.

Unknowingly, many dynasties have passed.

When I was taking pictures of the bronze man, a girl who looked like a Russian came towards me.

She also stopped in front of the same bronze statue and took pictures for a long time with her mobile phone.

We didn't say a word.

They just looked at each other, smiled, and nodded slightly.

Then, everyone continued to move forward.

Interesting and probably doesn’t need translation.

Make a complete circle and go back to look at the photo album.

Only then did I realize that what I took the most pictures of was not Gyeongpo Lake, lotus flowers, or the East China Sea.

But these people who can't move.

Later, I rode to the other side of the lake and met a huge moon again.

I pushed it seriously for a long time.

Of course, no push at all.

After leaving Gangneung, I still think of Gyeongpo Lake occasionally.

Don’t think of the lake first.

But those little copper figures.

In the last photo.

There are no missing bronze figures by Gyeongpo Lake.

There's just one more person pushing the moon.

title: Today, my liver is very layered
body:
Went to the Seoul Bar & Spirits Show on Sunday.

Five minutes after entering, I realized: Today, all drunkards in Seoul should be here.

With hundreds of booths, you can almost drink the world without a passport.

Moutai, Johnnie Walker, tequila, gin, vodka, Japanese whiskey...

Every few steps, someone handed me a small cup. The most dangerous sentence is: "Just one sip."

Because everyone says so.

So dozens of Just one sips finally made it into one afternoon.

Each wine has its own pairing: orange, chocolate, lime, kielbasa, cheese... I used to think they were afternoon tea. Today I discovered that they are actually responsible for defending every sip of wine:

"It's not spicy, it's layered."

"It's not a rush, it's a tail rhyme."

"It's not the boss, it's Hui Gan."

The staff are also very attentive. “Smell it first, then drink it, and feel the top, middle, and final notes.”

I nodded seriously. After drinking it, I began to suspect that it wasn’t that the wine was getting more complex, but that my tongue was getting more and more cooperative [Okay]

Every brand says: “Our wines are rich in layers.”

I later discovered that the real richness was in my liver. The upper layer is tequila, the middle layer is whiskey, and the bottom layer is Maotai. No one knows each other...

After more than two hours, I didn't feel dizzy at all.

I started to wonder if the bars in Seoul had trained me out this year [hehe]

Later I figured it out, it wasn’t my drinking that got better. Each brand is only responsible for getting you drunk a little bit, and everyone is particularly united.

Finally, today, the most sober people in Seoul are trying to prove that they are not drunk [faint]

Me too, but on the subway ride home, it seems to be swaying a little more rhythmically from side to side than usual. 🍸

title: Jiangneung Shipiao Village: The bridge is gone, but the home is still there
body:
Some people go to Gangneung for the sea, for coffee, to check in with BTS, and for the seaside of "Goblin".

But what really stopped me was an old house that many people barely knew about.

It's called Chuanqiao Village.

Three hundred years ago, this place was not called Chuanqiao Village. At that time, Gyeongpo Lake was much wider than it is today, and the water reached all the way to the front of the house. If you want to go home, there is no way, so you can only connect more than a dozen wooden boats one by one to serve as a bridge. People step on boats to go home, and the bridge sways gently with the water. Later, the lake receded, the boats were gone, and the bridge was gone. Only the three words "Chunqiao Village" were left, leaving a disappearing lake to future generations.

The owner of this house is Li Naifan.

History books barely write about him. There are no illustrious military exploits and no articles that have been passed down through the ages. It is only recorded that he built a house in Jiangling. There is a story among the people: When he was looking for a homestead, he saw a group of weasels slowly walking through the woods, and followed them all the way to Gyeongpo Lake. The wind stopped and the weasel stopped. He looked at the pine forest, the lake and the distant mountains, and just said: "It's right here."

Whether it is true or false, no one knows.

But many old houses have survived like this. History leaves facts, and stories leave warmth.

What I like most in Funaqiao Manor is not the main hall, but a small room called "Yuehuatang".

The word "happy words" doesn't make much sense.

Just talk cheerfully.

The owner built it not for lecturing or discussing politics, but for friends to come and have a place to drink tea, play chess, enjoy the snow, and spend the day slowly.

Standing there, I suddenly felt that the ancients understood the meaning of a house better than we do.

A house is not just a shelter from wind and rain.

It's still a place to wait for friends to come.

Three hundred years later, the Joseon Dynasty ended, Japanese colonization came, war came, and Gyeongpo Lake receded little by little. But Shipiao Village has never disappeared. Ten generations of people still live in the same courtyard. Children are born here, old people leave here, and the smoke never stops for a day.

When we left, the setting sun was setting into Gyeongpo Lake.

The yard was quiet except for the wind blowing through the pine trees.

I suddenly understood that what can really travel through time is never the carved buildings, but the fireworks in the world.

The bridge is gone.

The lake became smaller.

The dynasty has long gone.

But to this day, there are still people who open the door of this house and live under the same roof.

Perhaps the real legend of a house is not how much history it has experienced, but that no matter how things change, there are always people who are willing to go home.

title: 250 years, what is truly worth celebrating is not never making mistakes, but always having the ability to correct mistakes.
body:
250 has an unpleasant meaning in Chinese - "two hundred and five".

It just so happens that this year, the United States turns 250 years old.

When looking through history, I discovered an interesting coincidence: three presidents of the United States all died on July 4, Independence Day. Even more coincidentally, Jefferson and Adams - the main drafters of the Declaration of Independence - died on the same day, July 4, 1826, the 50th anniversary of Independence.

History sometimes writes better scripts than movies.

In the past 250 years, the United States has produced great presidents as well as controversial presidents. Almost every generation will feel: "Is this president a little unreliable?"

But after 250 years, I feel more and more that the true competitiveness of a country does not always select the best people.

But even if you choose the wrong person, you don’t have to start over.

The constitution is ironclad and the president is running water.

A truly mature system does not ensure that it is always correct, but makes it difficult for any one person to decide the fate of the entire country; it also gives every mistake a chance to be corrected.

Thinking of this, I started thinking about AI instead.

Over the past two hundred years, humans have continued to pursue higher productivity. For the first time, AI allows us to see that productivity may indeed achieve an order of magnitude jump.

But if AI ultimately only allows a few companies to have higher market values ​​and allows a few people to accumulate more wealth, then it is just an upgrade of capitalism.

I'd rather expect another outcome.

The productivity created by AI will not ultimately be deposited into the wealth of a few people, but will eventually be cashed into the time of the majority of people.

Work four days a week, or even three days; have more time to spend with your family, study, create, travel, or just relax.

The true meaning of technology should not be to make people busier and busier, but to give people the freedom to not have to be busy all the time.

250 years ago, what people fought for was political freedom.

Today, 250 years later, I hope that AI can bring another kind of freedom—the freedom of time.

Because the true success of a society is not about how many trillion-dollar companies it has, but whether ordinary people have more time for themselves.

title: Pathology never assumes that experts are infallible
body:
——In the AI era, I re-understand pathology

Today I was chatting with several eBay and TikTok e-commerce colleagues about platform governance and trust issues.

In seller management, a 3% false positive may accidentally injure a large number of high-quality sellers; while a false negative may cause huge consumer losses and platform trust risks. Everyone will naturally ask: Can AI solve it? Can the accuracy continue to improve?

As we were chatting, a friend was surprised to learn that I graduated from medical school and had done lymphoma, immunohistochemistry and molecular diagnosis in the pathology department of Beijing Medical University. This also reminded me of the days when Professor Gao Zifen took me to the pathology department.

When I was young, I always felt strange: Why did a case take so long to be discussed? Why immunohistochemistry panel OnePlusPlus? Why do experts still need to consult and argue with each other? Why are you always worried?

Looking back many years later, I slowly understood:

Pathology never assumes that experts are infallible.

On the contrary, it defaults to the fact that people will have disagreements, deviations, overconfidence, and even the entire group will slowly go astray without knowing it.

Therefore, consultation, double reading of films, immunohistochemistry, molecular diagnosis, digital pathology, external quality evaluation, and today's increasingly important pathology proficiency verification are essentially just extensions of the same philosophy at different stages.

The real problem they have to solve is never how to prove themselves right, but how to keep a complex system continuously calibrated.

The greatest successes of pathology proficiency testing are precisely those mistakes that never occur.

Taleb proposed Via Negativa in The Black Swan. People are accustomed to rewarding those results that have already happened, but rarely reward those things that did not happen because of prevention.

From this perspective, every problem discovered in a proficiency test means that a r…8724 tokens truncated…t turns another corner for you.

The day is over. After twists and turns, the discount is quite cheap.

Back home.

I looked at the heavy bag of dumplings and remembered what Buffett said: If you want to be happier, expect less.

I think what he said makes sense. At least, it makes sense today.I silently carried the bag of Michelin Big Mac dumplings downstairs.

Swipe your card, open the organic bin, and throw it in.

"Drip."

Deduction successful.

I stood there in silence for two seconds.

The last surprise today

To throw away the unpalatable Michelin, they actually charge a fee.

title: cool buddha
body:
I took my brother from Nishimura around for a weekend and stumbled into a very "serious"-looking Seoul International Buddhist Culture Exhibition.

I originally thought: Incense + Buddha beads + encourage people to do good.
As a result, there was a line of several hundred meters long at the door - and most of them were young Koreans.
We both looked at each other: something is wrong.

After entering, I found that my thinking was limited.

Buddha, you can wear a suit (it’s quite aura)
Monk, can dance (comparable to a girl group, but more joyful)
For peripherals, you can sell "INNER PEACE" T-shirts (8,000 won, I actually want to buy them)

There was an illusion for a moment——
What you walked into was not a Buddhist exhibition;
It’s Buddha pop-up scene

Confirm again:
South Korea’s exhibitions never follow common sense;
But aesthetics never fails.

Everyone is happy, and the happiness is written on their faces.

Suddenly I understood a little bit——
The so-called practice is not to stay away from the world;
It's about making the world more interesting.

Kpop can roll up the stage,
Bpop directly rolls "inner" #Seoul #BuddhismExpo #ExpatLife #Fun #Korea 🇰🇷

title: First time Kpop
body:
Out of a little bit of curiosity, and a little bit of obsession that "living in Korea without seeing a Kpop scene is incomplete", I went to Gyeongbokgung Palace today to watch a BTS comeback scene.

The media said there were 300,000 people, and the number of tourists from overseas had doubled. The number itself is magical - it's hard not to be drawn to it.

It started at 8pm and I arrived at around 4pm. Following the flow of people through the security check and walking to Gwanghwamun, the place was already full of seats. Everyone had an appointment slip in hand, and I only realized belatedly—it turned out to be an appointment 🙂
But now that I’m here, I’m not obsessed with the “best location.” Being smart (or maybe afraid of being tired), I found a cold drink shop next to the stands, went upstairs and ordered a cup of matcha.

So I had a "VIP perspective": not crowded, not hot, not noisy. Through the glass window, I watched the crowds outside gradually increase.

It's almost 8 o'clock, and the cup of matcha finally bottoms out. I walked downstairs and stood in the crowd. As soon as the lights turned on, the music started, and the cheers of the crowd pushed the atmosphere to its climax on time. There are many foreigners like me around, with various skin colors, mixed among Koreans.

After listening for a while, a very inappropriate sentence suddenly came to my mind:

that’s it? [arrogance]

Such a famous boy band, this? [Depreciation]
Are my expectations too high, or do I have some misunderstanding about Kpop?

I started observing the people around me:
There were some who were very high, and there were also many who stood quietly like me.

Now that you are here, just listen to the end. Maybe one of them will impress me.

As a result, I really persisted until the end.
My legs are numb, and I feel a little regretful. I feel like I was deceived by the "famous name" for an afternoon and an evening. [vomit]

On the stage were a few little boys who didn’t fit my “manly” stereotype. They sang content that I didn’t quite understand, and the rhythm and melody didn’t hit me. They danced hard and performed hard, but to me, that’s about it.

On the way back, I suddenly remembered a book I was listening to during the day: The Social Animal.

It talks about two things:

First, it is easy for people to follow blindly.
Second, our aesthetics and judgments are essentially deeply shaped by past experiences.

Today, these two points were thoroughly verified for me.

Why did I come?
Because labels such as "300,000 people" and "world's top" are themselves a kind of guidance. It can even be said to be a kind of mild "group pressure." This is blind obedience.

So why don't I like it?Because I am used to listening to Jazz, Blue, Country, Rock, French and even Disney, or those more "diva-like" sounds; my understanding of "masculinity" has long been framed by past experiences.
So I'm not listening to music, I'm using my own coordinate system to judge something in a completely different system.

The result is of course: not understanding, not even recognizing.

But the problem isn’t with it, and it’s not entirely with me.
It's just a perception.

So perhaps a closer conclusion is:

everything is just as is.
It’s not about whether it’s good or bad, it’s about which coordinate system you look at it from.

The significance of this afternoon, when I thought about it later, was not that I "finally checked in to a Kpop scene" and added another check to my life list.
But it made me realize again:

Self-righteous people who think that they are rational and independent judges,
But in essence, it is just an ordinary "social animal".

I will probably remind myself more in the future:
When I have a strong judgment, I might as well ask:
Is this true, or is it just my perspective? #KpopFirst Experience #Social Animal #Self-Awareness #Prejudice and Blind Obedience

title: People think experience will tell the answer, but in fact it just repeats prejudice - Third Millennium Thinking
body:
When traveling to and from the United States and South Korea, every time I feel like my body, mind, and memory are being torn apart and placed in different spaces. My body is still at home in Seattle, my thoughts are floating quietly on the Pacific clouds, and my subconscious has quietly started to prepare for the bombardment of the Korean-speaking world. In fact, this itself is my definition of narrow space - from a space perspective, where are the boundaries of continents and countries? It’s just a small blue planet, with an even more insignificant me floating on it

After reading "Third Millennium Thinking" along the way, the author gathered together: Nobel Prize winner in physics Saul Perlmutter, philosopher John Campbell, psychologist Robert MacCoun

The authors have been collaborating on an interdisciplinary course at the University of California, Berkeley, since 2011, with the goal of helping students learn what scientific thinking is; to distinguish between fact, fiction, and opinion in an age of information explosion; to learn to ask the right questions in complex problems rather than jumping to conclusions; to use probabilistic thinking, evidential logic, and critical thinking to solve problems; and to collaborate with people with different viewpoints rather than talking to themselves in the stratosphere.

They integrate the core tools of physics, philosophy and psychology to form a thinking framework that can be used in daily life, decision-making and public issues. It is especially suitable for the era of information explosion and complex reality.

There is a short story in the book:

When Saul Perlmutter was doing postdoc, the team caught up with a once-in-a-million opportunity: Supernova 1987A exploded, leaving behind a neutron star with a neutron star pulse of up to 2000Hz. The team flew to Chile for observation, and the high-sensitivity telescope captured the pulse, but the frequency seemed unstable. After Doppler correction, a perfect sine wave appeared! It was once thought that a neutron star exoplanet had been discovered, and it was directly published in Nature. If it ended like this, it would be a brilliant career move.

The next year, they wanted to write another Nature article and wait for further observations. The pulses were missing and missing, which was related to the switch of the instrument on the other side of the mountain. Finally, it was discovered that the telescope was too sensitive and captured the weak signal leaked by the instrument. After correction, it was "made up" into a perfect sine wave.
In other words, they didn't actually discover the planet. To be honest, they can only withdraw the manuscript from Nature.Science is about finding patterns, testing, failing, correcting, and slowly building understanding.
Real science is the process of finding patterns, testing, failing, revising, and slowly building understanding.

Here are some excerpts from the essay that reminded me:

1. I thought I was thinking, but in fact I was just repeating the story I wanted to hear.
2. Experts are not always right. Truly trustworthy experts are often those who are willing to show their weaknesses and revise their opinions.
3. Don’t think of the problem as right/wrong, but use probabilistic thinking to measure confidence and uncertainty.
4. Disagreement is not animosity but an opportunity to discover new directions.
5. Knowing what you don’t know is more reliable than being rash and confident. Doubt is not pessimism, but the courage to admit that we simply don’t know the answer.

I hope that I will often ask these questions in the future:

1. Is every piece of information and every choice around me facts, or is it the story I want to see?
2. When everyone nods in unison, do you dare to stop and ask: Is it really right?
3. When you see a piece of data, story, or trend that seems to be a “perfect pattern”, should you treat it as a signal or check whether it may come from noise?
4. How confident are you in a certain point of view? Have you tried describing my confidence level in terms of probabilities?

🎬【Soorarai Pottru】Heroic Hymn

I don’t care much about Indian movies, but this movie released by Amazon Prime Video in 2020 shocked me

The film is based on the life story of G.R. Gopinath, the founder of Indian low-cost airline Air Deccan, as described in his memoir "Simply Fly: A Deccan Odyssey"

The protagonist left home for many years when he was young due to conflicting ideas with his father's fighting methods.
Years later, the father and son finally reconciled, but when his father was in danger, he was stopped at the airport with the words "Economy class is sold out."
After he failed to seek help but was escorted out of the airport by security guards, he used various means of transportation to rush home. When his father was dying, he hallucinated his son in military uniform, but it was just a fantasy. By the time he got home, his father had already been cremated.

The story is not a dramatic effect, but the coldest truth about India:
The poor have to fight hard for even the basic rights of "access", but they can't get it.

This huge regret made him decide to do something that everyone thought was ridiculous:Make it possible for ordinary people to fly

The movie restores the road ahead so cruelly that the audience will feel suffocated in despair:
Suppression by giants, institutional restrictions, credit traps, bureaucratic delays, and security crises
He was knocked down time and time again, but he got up again and again.

What really moved me was the warmth surrounding him:
His mother quietly put years of savings into his hands;
The wife supports her shaky life by selling bread;
Friends carried him when he was at his most desperate;
Even officers who once hated denying him stood up to support him at critical moments.

There is great evil in the world, but the good in people's hearts is never absent.
It was these broken lights that pushed him forward step after step every time he was desperate.

When the plane that truly belongs to ordinary people takes off,
That's not victory,
But a very quiet answer that changes the world

What truly stayed with me was this:

We aren’t defined by how many times we fall,
but by the one more time we choose to rise.

Fear doesn’t disappear -
we simply grow bigger than it.

Nothing we’ve suffered through is wasted.
Every failure secretly prepares the ground beneath our next step.

And ordinary people,
when they refuse to give up,
quietly bend the world toward fairness.

This film is a reminder - for anyone struggling, doubting, or scared -
there is always one more step forward waiting for you. Go for it!

title: small street
body:
A year ago, I would never have thought of this.
One day, because of the anxiety of recruiting 40,000 e-commerce sellers in four weeks, I will be alone in Gangnam, Seoul, on the other side of the world, walking around in an ordinary alley.

I never thought the Monday night party would be so beautiful -
There are almost ripe persimmons growing on the branches on the roadside, red lanterns in cute izakayas, New York Bagel bakery, Irish bars with Christmas trees lit up, Thai restaurants, fried food stalls... and various quirky and cute restaurants.
I feel like this Minxiang is comforting me: "Don't think about it, just eat something first."

Some answers may not depend on thinking,
By walking, by smelling the fragrance on the street,
Or be silently healed by a bunch of persimmons.

If you're in a bad mood, you need to take a walk.
If you're in a good mood, go for a walk.
As you walk you will find,
Sometimes life is like this alley, the destination is not important,
Beautiful scenery is hidden in those few steps you didn’t plan

And the so-called relaxation is probably on an ordinary Monday night,
Not in a hurry, not in a hurry, not even in a hurry,
Just walk around according to your mood and you can encounter a whole street of romance

Take your time, there will always be a solution - there are always more solutions than difficulties [Come on]

title: Late night in Seoul·An unexpected journey started by a poster
body:
After reading for a day, I felt tired. In the evening, I went to a nearby church to listen to music and donate some money. On the way out of the church, the night breeze was just right. I was walking slowly home, and my eyes were instantly caught by a big red BEST MUSICAL poster on the side of the road - the color scheme, the momentum, it was clearly the tone of Broadway.

Being naturally curious, I quickly took a closer look - it turned out to be "Moulin Rouge"! It's the kind that just opened in Seoul. The poster said "Blue Square", and I kept walking forward as I thought to myself, "Where is this?"

Then something magical happened:

title: cool buddha
body:
I took my brother from Nishimura around for a weekend and stumbled into a very "serious"-looking Seoul International Buddhist Culture Exhibition.

I originally thought: Incense + Buddha beads + encourage people to do good.
As a result, there was a line of several hundred meters long at the door - and most of them were young Koreans.
We both looked at each other: something is wrong.

After entering, I found that my thinking was limited.

Buddha, you can wear a suit (it’s quite aura)
Monk, can dance (comparable to a girl group, but more joyful)
For peripherals, you can sell "INNER PEACE" T-shirts (8,000 won, I actually want to buy them)

There was an illusion for a moment——
What you walked into was not a Buddhist exhibition;
It’s Buddha pop-up scene

Confirm again:
South Korea’s exhibitions never follow common sense;
But aesthetics never fails.

Everyone is happy, and the happiness is written on their faces.

Suddenly I understood a little bit——
The so-called practice is not to stay away from the world;
It's about making the world more interesting.

Kpop can roll up the stage,
Bpop directly rolls "inner" #Seoul #BuddhismExpo #ExpatLife #Fun #Korea 🇰🇷

title: First time Kpop
body:
Out of a little bit of curiosity, and a little bit of obsession that "living in Korea without seeing a Kpop scene is incomplete", I went to Gyeongbokgung Palace today to watch a BTS comeback scene.

The media said there were 300,000 people, and the number of tourists from overseas had doubled. The number itself is magical - it's hard not to be drawn to it.

It started at 8pm and I arrived at around 4pm. Following the flow of people through the security check and walking to Gwanghwamun, the place was already full of seats. Everyone had an appointment slip in hand, and I only realized belatedly—it turned out to be an appointment 🙂
But now that I’m here, I’m not obsessed with the “best location.” Being smart (or maybe afraid of being tired), I found a cold drink shop next to the stands, went upstairs and ordered a cup of matcha.

So I had a "VIP perspective": not crowded, not hot, not noisy. Through the glass window, I watched the crowds outside gradually increase.

It's almost 8 o'clock, and the cup of matcha finally bottoms out. I walked downstairs and stood in the crowd. As soon as the lights turned on, the music started, and the cheers of the crowd pushed the atmosphere to its climax on time. There are many foreigners like me around, with various skin colors, mixed among Koreans.

After listening for a while, a very inappropriate sentence suddenly came to my mind:

that’s it? [arrogance]

Such a famous boy band, this? [Depreciation]
Are my expectations too high, or do I have some misunderstanding about Kpop?

I started observing the people around me:
There were some who were very high, and there were also many who stood quietly like me.

Now that you are here, just listen to the end. Maybe one of them will impress me.

As a result, I really persisted until the end.
My legs are numb, and I feel a little regretful. I feel like I was deceived by the "famous name" for an afternoon and an evening. [vomit]

On the stage were a few little boys who didn’t fit my “manly” stereotype. They sang content that I didn’t quite understand, and the rhythm and melody didn’t hit me. They danced hard and performed hard, but to me, that’s about it.

On the way back, I suddenly remembered a book I was listening to during the day: The Social Animal.

It talks about two things:

First, it is easy for people to follow blindly.
Second, our aesthetics and judgments are essentially deeply shaped by past experiences.

Today, these two points were thoroughly verified for me.

Why did I come?
Because labels such as "300,000 people" and "world's top" are themselves a kind of guidance. It can even be said to be a kind of mild "group pressure." This is blind obedience.

So why don't I like it?Because I am used to listening to Jazz, Blue, Country, Rock, French and even Disney, or those more "diva-like" sounds; my understanding of "masculinity" has long been framed by past experiences.
So I'm not listening to music, I'm using my own coordinate system to judge something in a completely different system.

The result is of course: not understanding, not even recognizing.

But the problem isn’t with it, and it’s not entirely with me.
It's just a perception.

So perhaps a closer conclusion is:

everything is just as is.
It’s not about whether it’s good or bad, it’s about which coordinate system you look at it from.

The significance of this afternoon, when I thought about it later, was not that I "finally checked in to a Kpop scene" and added another check to my life list.
But it made me realize again:

Self-righteous people who think that they are rational and independent judges,
But in essence, it is just an ordinary "social animal".

I will probably remind myself more in the future:
When I have a strong judgment, I might as well ask:
Is this true, or is it just my perspective? #KpopFirst Experience #Social Animal #Self-Awareness #Prejudice and Blind Obedience

title: People think experience will tell the answer, but in fact it just repeats prejudice - Third Millennium Thinking
body:
When traveling to and from the United States and South Korea, every time I feel like my body, mind, and memory are being torn apart and placed in different spaces. My body is still at home in Seattle, my thoughts are floating quietly on the Pacific clouds, and my subconscious has quietly started to prepare for the bombardment of the Korean-speaking world. In fact, this itself is my definition of narrow space - from a space perspective, where are the boundaries of continents and countries? It’s just a small blue planet, with an even more insignificant me floating on it

After reading "Third Millennium Thinking" along the way, the author gathered together: Nobel Prize winner in physics Saul Perlmutter, philosopher John Campbell, psychologist Robert MacCoun

The authors have been collaborating on an interdisciplinary course at the University of California, Berkeley, since 2011, with the goal of helping students learn what scientific thinking is; to distinguish between fact, fiction, and opinion in an age of information explosion; to learn to ask the right questions in complex problems rather than jumping to conclusions; to use probabilistic thinking, evidential logic, and critical thinking to solve problems; and to collaborate with people with different viewpoints rather than talking to themselves in the stratosphere.

They integrate the core tools of physics, philosophy and psychology to form a thinking framework that can be used in daily life, decision-making and public issues. It is especially suitable for the era of information explosion and complex reality.

There is a short story in the book:

When Saul Perlmutter was doing postdoc, the team caught up with a once-in-a-million opportunity: Supernova 1987A exploded, leaving behind a neutron star with a neutron star pulse of up to 2000Hz. The team flew to Chile for observation, and the high-sensitivity telescope captured the pulse, but the frequency seemed unstable. After Doppler correction, a perfect sine wave appeared! It was once thought that a neutron star exoplanet had been discovered, and it was directly published in Nature. If it ended like this, it would be a brilliant career move.

The next year, they wanted to write another Nature article and wait for further observations. The pulses were missing and missing, which was related to the switch of the instrument on the other side of the mountain. Finally, it was discovered that the telescope was too sensitive and captured the weak signal leaked by the instrument. After correction, it was "made up" into a perfect sine wave.
In other words, they didn't actually discover the planet. To be honest, they can only withdraw the manuscript from Nature.Science is about finding patterns, testing, failing, correcting, and slowly building understanding.
Real science is the process of finding patterns, testing, failing, revising, and slowly building understanding.

Here are some excerpts from the essay that reminded me:

1. I thought I was thinking, but in fact I was just repeating the story I wanted to hear.
2. Experts are not always right. Truly trustworthy experts are often those who are willing to show their weaknesses and revise their opinions.
3. Don’t think of the problem as right/wrong, but use probabilistic thinking to measure confidence and uncertainty.
4. Disagreement is not animosity but an opportunity to discover new directions.
5. Knowing what you don’t know is more reliable than being rash and confident. Doubt is not pessimism, but the courage to admit that we simply don’t know the answer.

I hope that I will often ask these questions in the future:

1. Is every piece of information and every choice around me facts, or is it the story I want to see?
2. When everyone nods in unison, do you dare to stop and ask: Is it really right?
3. When you see a piece of data, story, or trend that seems to be a “perfect pattern”, should you treat it as a signal or check whether it may come from noise?
4. How confident are you in a certain point of view? Have you tried describing my confidence level in terms of probabilities?

🎬【Soorarai Pottru】Heroic Hymn

I don’t care much about Indian movies, but this movie released by Amazon Prime Video in 2020 shocked me

The film is based on the life story of G.R. Gopinath, the founder of Indian low-cost airline Air Deccan, as described in his memoir "Simply Fly: A Deccan Odyssey"

The protagonist left home for many years when he was young due to conflicting ideas with his father's fighting methods.
Years later, the father and son finally reconciled, but when his father was in danger, he was stopped at the airport with the words "Economy class is sold out."
After he failed to seek help but was escorted out of the airport by security guards, he used various means of transportation to rush home. When his father was dying, he hallucinated his son in military uniform, but it was just a fantasy. By the time he got home, his father had already been cremated.

The story is not a dramatic effect, but the coldest truth about India:
The poor have to fight hard for even the basic rights of "access", but they can't get it.

This huge regret made him decide to do something that everyone thought was ridiculous:Make it possible for ordinary people to fly

The movie restores the road ahead so cruelly that the audience will feel suffocated in despair:
Suppression by giants, institutional restrictions, credit traps, bureaucratic delays, and security crises
He was knocked down time and time again, but he got up again and again.

What really moved me was the warmth surrounding him:
His mother quietly put years of savings into his hands;
The wife supports her shaky life by selling bread;
Friends carried him when he was at his most desperate;
Even officers who once hated denying him stood up to support him at critical moments.

There is great evil in the world, but the good in people's hearts is never absent.
It was these broken lights that pushed him forward step after step every time he was desperate.

When the plane that truly belongs to ordinary people takes off,
That's not victory,
But a very quiet answer that changes the world

What truly stayed with me was this:

We aren’t defined by how many times we fall,
but by the one more time we choose to rise.

Fear doesn’t disappear -
we simply grow bigger than it.

Nothing we’ve suffered through is wasted.
Every failure secretly prepares the ground beneath our next step.

And ordinary people,
when they refuse to give up,
quietly bend the world toward fairness.

This film is a reminder - for anyone struggling, doubting, or scared -
there is always one more step forward waiting for you. Go for it!

title: small street
body:
A year ago, I would never have thought of this.
One day, because of the anxiety of recruiting 40,000 e-commerce sellers in four weeks, I will be alone in Gangnam, Seoul, on the other side of the world, walking around in an ordinary alley.

I never thought the Monday night party would be so beautiful -
There are almost ripe persimmons growing on the branches on the roadside, red lanterns in cute izakayas, New York Bagel bakery, Irish bars with Christmas trees lit up, Thai restaurants, fried food stalls... and various quirky and cute restaurants.
I feel like this Minxiang is comforting me: "Don't think about it, just eat something first."

Some answers may not depend on thinking,
By walking, by smelling the fragrance on the street,
Or be silently healed by a bunch of persimmons.

If you're in a bad mood, you need to take a walk.
If you're in a good mood, go for a walk.
As you walk you will find,
Sometimes life is like this alley, the destination is not important,
Beautiful scenery is hidden in those few steps you didn’t plan

And the so-called relaxation is probably on an ordinary Monday night,
Not in a hurry, not in a hurry, not even in a hurry,
Just walk around according to your mood and you can encounter a whole street of romance

Take your time, there will always be a solution - there are always more solutions than difficulties [Come on]
